definition: A model's ability to maintain reliable performance when faced with noisy, out-of-distribution, or adversarially perturbed inputs.
details: Robustness is a key concern for deploying models in real-world settings, where inputs will inevitably differ from the clean, curated data seen during training and evaluation.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. Think of it this way: A model's ability to maintain reliable performance when faced with noisy, out-of-distribution, or adversarially perturbed inputs. And here is the clever part: Robustness is a key concern for deploying models in real-world settings, where inputs will inevitably differ from the clean, curated data seen during training and evaluation. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. And that is Robustness — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
